question: The company Altri SGPS S.A. has formally announced its plans to set up a soluble cellulose and lyocell factory in Palas de Rei (Galicia, Spain). To do so, it intends to raise EUR 250 million in public funding through the PERTE (strategic project for economic recovery and transformation) for industrial decarbonisation.
The impacts of this activity include the emission of sulphur oxides and nitrous oxides, which will cause acid rain within a 10-30 km radius of the factory and affect biomass and human health.

With regard to the implementation of the new Air Quality Directive and the DNSH principle, which makes it mandatory to consider direct and indirect effects of an activity throughout its life cycle, the project does not consider the potential health effects of its emissions, although it does acknowledge the emission of environmental pollutants, including nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxide and others.

These emissions are the main cause of the harmful effects on human health and the local population produced throughout the life cycle of the activity. To the extent that this constitutes a breach of the DNSH principle and that this activity is at odds with the new directive, can this project be eligible for funding?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.5.2024) In the context of the Recovery and Resilience Facility, the Commission has not yet received any payment request from Spain that required the assessment of the cellulose and lyocell factory in Palas de Rei (Galicia, Spain).

Regarding the ‘do no significant harm’ (DNSH), the measures related to PERTES (strategic project for economic recovery and transformation) in the Recovery and Resilience Plan of Spain require that selection criteria ensure compliance with the DNSH principle and national and EU environmental legislation, including the new air quality directive.

The fulfilment of the targets related to the PERTES as well as the DNSH requirements and the compliance with environmental legislation in place will be formally assessed by the Commission under the relevant payment requests. The Commission has a regular dialogue with the Member States to monitor the implementation of the milestones and targets in the Recovery and Resilience Plan, including DNSH related requirements.
